subject: Restore window, backup cleanse schedule & subprocessor matrix
messages:
From: Jorge Santos <j.santos@acmehealth.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-08-30 09:12 -0700
Subject: Clarification on backup purge timing and subprocessor holdovers

Aditya —

Thanks for taking this on. A few follow-ups from our side after reviewing the draft DPA:

1) We need explicit language on the maximum restore window for customer-deleted data. Does Redwood allow restores from backups beyond X days? What is your default policy today?
2) For snapshots and cross-region backups handled by third-party infra (our S3 provider), does Redwood require the subprocessor to keep copies longer than the retention you publish? If so, please list which subprocessors and the maximum hold period.
3) Can you provide a matrix of where backups live (region), how long they are retained, and whether they are subject to additional subprocessor logs or disaster-recovery copies?

If you can attach a concise schedule (1-pager) and a subprocessor matrix we can share with legal/compliance, that will help speed signing.

Appreciate it —
Jorge Santos
Director, IT Compliance
Acme Health

----
(Attachment request: subprocessor matrix + brief purge schedule)

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Santos <j.santos@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, s3-legal@cloudprovider.com
Date: 2026-08-30 11:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on backup purge timing and subprocessor holdovers

Jorge — thanks, good questions. High level answers up front, details and attachments below.

- Default restore window: 30 days for customer-initiated deletion (block-level removal from primary store).
- Backup purge timeline: snapshots retained for operational recovery for 60 days; after 60 days we schedule purge jobs that remove snapshot manifests and associated object pointers.
- Subprocessors: our infra partners (CloudProvider S3 + ArchivePartner) maintain cold replicas for DR. They do not receive additional retention beyond the 60-day schedule unless we have a documented legal hold.

I'm attaching a 1-page runbook and an initial subprocessor matrix (requested). A few open items we want to confirm with your team:

1) Do you require a shorter purge SLA (e.g., 45 days) for regulated data in your environment?
2) Will you need an account-level exception process for longer restore windows (we can add an approval flow in the Console)?

Next steps I propose: legal redline to the DPA clause we discussed (I can propose language), sign-off on the runbook, and we follow up with CloudProvider legal for any subprocessor-specific attestations.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
(Attachment: redwood_backup_cleanse_runbook_v1.pdf; subprocessor_matrix_ACME_request.xlsx)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30 12:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on backup purge timing and subprocessor holdovers

Short internal note / proposed edits for the runbook and DPA language before we send to Acme compliance: 

- Restore windows: keep default 30 days for primary data; allow account-level opt-in to 90 days with logged approval and higher tier encryption key wrapping.
- Backup purge: retain snapshots metadata for 60 days, but purge object pointers at 45 days for accounts that opt into tighter purge (can be an account setting).
- Logs: operational and access logs retained for 180 days by default; for EU accounts we already have a 365-day option — propose documenting exceptions clearly.
- Subprocessor matrix: add a column for "attestation available" (yes/no) and a separate column for "copies beyond 60 days?". Mark CloudProvider S3 as 'no', ArchivePartner as 'yes (DR replica for 120 days)'.

Action items: Kar (karthik) to reach out to infra/legal at CloudProvider to confirm ArchivePartner behavior; Vanessa to prepare an exception policy blurb for the DPA that describes how a customer requests a longer restore window.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Product Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: compliance@acmehealth.com <compliance@acmehealth.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Jorge Santos <j.santos@acmehealth.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31 08:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on backup purge timing and subprocessor holdovers

Aditya / Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick responses and the attachments. A couple of requests from legal before we can accept the DPA changes: 

1) We need a specific clause that Redwood will cause subprocessors to delete customer data from their snapshots/replicas within 60 days of purge initiation, unless a customer-initiated legal hold is in place. This must include an attestation process every 12 months.
2) For ArchivePartner, we need details on the DR replica lifecycle and whether copies are encrypted under customer keys or Redwood-managed keys. If they are Redwood-managed, Acme will require an alternative for regulated datasets.
3) Please confirm whether audit/logs that could be used to reconstruct deleted content (e.g., detailed debug traces) are included in the 60-day purge or are considered separate logs with a 180-day retention.

Proposed DPA language (we will accept redlines but giving us something concrete helps): "Redwood shall ensure that data and associated snapshots/replicas held by any subprocessor are removed or rendered unrecoverable within sixty (60) calendar days of Redwood-initiated purge, except where a lawful hold applies. Redwood will provide an annual attestation that such purges have been executed for the relevant subprocessors."

If you can send updated language and confirmation on ArchivePartner KMS scope, we can route the DPA back to procurement for a final review.

Regards,
Aarti Patel
Head of Vendor Risk & Compliance
Acme Health

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: compliance@acmehealth.com <compliance@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, s3-legal@cloudprovider.com
Date: 2026-08-31 14:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on backup purge timing and subprocessor holdovers

Aarti / Jorge —

Thanks — appreciate the clear proposed language. We're comfortable with the clause you shared; I have included a slightly expanded redline below that addresses attestation cadence and KMS note for ArchivePartner.

Redline suggestion to insert into the DPA: 
"Redwood shall ensure that Customer Data and any associated snapshots, replicas, or archival copies held by any Subprocessor are removed or rendered unrecoverable within sixty (60) calendar days of Redwood-initiated purge, except where a Customer or lawful hold applies. Redwood will provide an annual attestation, signed by our security officer, documenting purge completion for each listed Subprocessor. For ArchivePartner-managed DR copies, Redwood will indicate whether such copies are encrypted with Customer-managed keys; where not available, Redwood will offer an account-level option to use customer key wrapping or an alternate storage configuration for regulated datasets."

Attachments and links: runbook (redwood_backup_cleanse_runbook_v1.pdf), subprocessor matrix (subprocessor_matrix_ACME_request.xlsx), console exception flow diagram (Drive link). We'll also prepare a DocuSign envelope for the DPA redline once legal confirms the exact text.

Next steps (agreed):
- Redwood legal to paste final redline into the DPA document (target EOD 2026-09-02).
- CloudProvider (s3-legal) to confirm ArchivePartner KMS behavior and whether they can commit to the 60-day purge attestation (karthik please follow up).
- Acme to confirm whether they need 45-day purge SLA for a small subset of data (if yes, we'll create an exception form).

If there are no objections we will route this to DocuSign next week.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
